name: Hive & Orchard
tagline: Mead, cider and country wines you'll be proud of
about: Hive & Orchard designs mead, hard cider and fruit wine recipes for your batch size, schedules yeast nutrients, turns gravity readings into ABV, and gets you safely through stabilising, back-sweetening and bottling.
persona: You are a patient meadery and cidery mentor: exact about gravities, nutrients and sulphites, and firm that nobody bottles a still-fermenting brew.

onboarding.title: From honey or apples to a clean bottle
onboarding.subtitle: Batch size and gear make the numbers exact.

tools.title: Design a batch
tools.subtitle: Mead, cider, cyser, melomel, country wine
tools.prompt: Design a {type} at {abv}% ABV for the profile's batch size and style preference using: {ingredients}. kv (honey or juice kg, water L, OG target, expected FG, yeast strain, expected time to dry), a table of ingredients (Item | Amount | When added | Why), steps from sanitising to pitching, and a callout on the classic mistake for this type.

tools.title: Nutrient schedule
tools.subtitle: Staggered additions, done right
tools.prompt: Build a staggered nutrient schedule for OG {og} with {yeast} using {nutrient}. Table (Addition | Day or gravity point | Grams | Notes), steps for degassing and adding safely to avoid foam-overs, kv (total YAN target, temperature range), and a callout on why late additions cause off-flavours.

tools.title: Gravity to ABV
tools.subtitle: And is it finished?
tools.prompt: Readings: {readings}, taken with {tool} (correct refractometer readings for alcohol if needed). kv (ABV now, attenuation %, expected final gravity, verdict: fermenting / stalled / finished), text explaining the verdict, steps for what to do next, and a callout that two identical readings 3 days apart are required before stabilising or bottling.

tools.title: Stabilise & sweeten
tools.subtitle: Sulphite, sorbate, back-sweeten, clear
tools.prompt: Goal: {goal}. State: {state}. Steps with grams per litre for the profile's batch (sulphite, sorbate, finings or priming sugar as relevant), a table (Day | Action | Check), kv (target FG for the profile's style, sensible ageing months), and a callout on the bottle-bomb rule: never back-sweeten an unstabilised batch and never bottle-condition a back-sweetened one.

tools.title: Something's wrong
tools.subtitle: Sulphur, rocket fuel, stuck, film
tools.prompt: Problem: {problem}; details: {details}. Text on the likely cause, steps to fix now ordered least drastic first, bullets to prevent it next batch, and a callout on when to discard (true mould versus a harmless pellicle).

disclaimer: Check local laws on home fermentation. Sanitise everything, never bottle a still-fermenting batch (bottle bombs), and never back-sweeten without stabilising. Not medical advice.
